# Research Question

Opinions of political candidates have long been associated with specific attitudinal and demographic characteristics. Foundational work by Campbell et al. (1960) established party identification as a relatively stable predictor of voter choice and political attitudes. Achen and Bartels (2016), through their group theory of democracy, emphasize the importance of social group identities and demographic characteristics in shaping political preferences. Additionally, work by Fiorina and Abramowitz has examined the relationship between political ideology, partisan identification, and political polarization.

Previous research on political behavior suggests that geographic location and regional political environments are associated with differences in political attitudes and partisan support. Because the ANES sampling design uses geographically based pseudo-clusters and strata, these identifiers provide an opportunity to examine whether Republican presidential candidate feeling thermometer ratings vary across sampling clusters, beyond the variation observed between individual respondents.

Using the 2016–2024 ANES panel, this project will employ a three-level longitudinal model to examine differences in baseline Republican candidate feeling thermometer ratings across clusters and individuals, as well as changes in these ratings across election cycles.

**Research Question:** To what extent do geographically based sampling clusters and individual differences account for variation in Republican presidential candidate feeling thermometer ratings, and how do trajectories of these ratings vary across the 2016, 2020, and 2024 election cycles?

```{r}
# Read full ANES panel data
library(tidyverse)

anes_panel_full <- read_csv(
  "ANES_Panel_Full.csv",
  na = c("", " ", "NA"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```


```{r}
# Select variables needed 
anes_selected <- anes_panel_full %>%
  select(

    # Respondent / Case IDs
    V160001_orig,   # Stable 2016 respondent ID
    V160001,        # 2016 case ID

    # Sample / interview completion status
    V160502,        # 2016 pre/post completion
    V200003,        # 2020 sample type
    V200004,        # 2020 pre/post completion
    V240003,        # 2024 sample type
    V240002c,       # 2024 pre/post completion
    
    # PRE Trump Feeling Thermometer
    V161087,        # 2016
    V201152,        # 2020
    V241157,        # 2024

    # POST Trump Feeling Thermometer
    V162079,        # 2016
    V202144,        # 2020
    V242126,        # 2024

    # PRE Party of Registration
    # Don't use POST here since so many NAs in 2024
    V161019,        # 2016
    V201018,        # 2020
    V241025,        # 2024

    # Race / Ethnicity
    V161310x,       # 2016
    V201549x,       # 2020
    V241501x,       # 2024

    # PRE Liberal-Conservative Self-Placement
    # Don't use POST here since we only have 2016 data
    V161126,        # 2016
    V201200,        # 2020
    V241177,        # 2024

    # Respondent Gender / Sex
    V161342,        # 2016
    V201600,        # 2020
    V241550,        # 2024

    # State
    V161010d,       # 2016 FIPS state
    V203000,        # 2020 FIPS state
    V243002,        # 2024 FIPS state

    # PRE / POST Weights
    V160101,        # 2016 PRE weight
    V160102,        # 2016 POST weight

    V200011a,       # 2020 panel PRE weight
    V200011b,       # 2020 panel POST weight

    V240106a,       # 2024 panel PRE weight
    V240106b,       # 2024 panel POST weight

    # PSU / Stratum
    V160201,        # 2016 Stratum – Full sample 
    V160202,        # 2016 Variance PSU – full sample 

    V200011c,       # 2020 panel variance unit
    V200011d,       # 2020 panel variance stratum

    V240106c,       # 2024 panel PSU
    V240106d,       # 2024 panel stratum
    
    # Additional 2024 Full-Sample PSU / Stratum
    V240108c,       # 2024 Full-sample PSU
    V240108d        # 2024 Full-sample Stratum
  ) %>%

    # Create 2024 Full-Sample Cluster ID
mutate(
  cluster_full_2024 = 1000 * (
    as.numeric(V240108c) + as.numeric(V240108d)
  )
)
```


```{r}
# Convert ANES panel from Wide to long format

anes_long <- anes_selected %>%

  # Standardize variable types before reshaping
  mutate(
    across(
      -c(V160001_orig, V160001),
      ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(.x))))
    )
  ) %>%

  # Rename variables to common names across years
  rename(

    # Interview completion status
    completion_status_2016 = V160502,
    completion_status_2020 = V200004,
    completion_status_2024 = V240002c,

    # Sample type
    sample_type_2020 = V200003,
    sample_type_2024 = V240003,

    # PRE Trump Feeling Thermometer
    trump_ft_pre_2016 = V161087,
    trump_ft_pre_2020 = V201152,
    trump_ft_pre_2024 = V241157,

    # POST Trump Feeling Thermometer
    trump_ft_post_2016 = V162079,
    trump_ft_post_2020 = V202144,
    trump_ft_post_2024 = V242126,

    # PRE Party of Registration
    party_reg_pre_2016 = V161019,
    party_reg_pre_2020 = V201018,
    party_reg_pre_2024 = V241025,

    # Race / Ethnicity
    race_2016 = V161310x,
    race_2020 = V201549x,
    race_2024 = V241501x,

    # PRE Liberal-Conservative Self-Placement
    ideology_pre_2016 = V161126,
    ideology_pre_2020 = V201200,
    ideology_pre_2024 = V241177,

    # Respondent Gender / Sex
    gender_2016 = V161342,
    gender_2020 = V201600,
    gender_2024 = V241550,

    # State
    state_fips_2016 = V161010d,
    state_fips_2020 = V203000,
    state_fips_2024 = V243002,

    # PRE Weights
    weight_pre_2016 = V160101,
    weight_pre_2020 = V200011a,
    weight_pre_2024 = V240106a,

    # POST Weights
    weight_post_2016 = V160102,
    weight_post_2020 = V200011b,
    weight_post_2024 = V240106b,

    # PSU
    psu_2016 = V160202,
    psu_2020 = V200011c,
    psu_2024 = V240106c,

    # Stratum
    stratum_2016 = V160201,
    stratum_2020 = V200011d,
    stratum_2024 = V240106d,
    
    # Additional 2024 Full-Sample PSU / Stratum
    psu_full_2024 = V240108c,
    stratum_full_2024 = V240108d
  ) %>%
  
  # Convert wide format into long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(V160001_orig, V160001),
    names_to = c(".value", "year"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(2016|2020|2024)$",
    names_transform = list(year = as.integer),
    values_drop_na = FALSE
  ) %>%

  # Sort by respondent and year
  arrange(V160001, year)
```

### Histogram by Year
```{r descriptive stats}
ggplot(data = anes_cleaned) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(y = V162079)) +
  labs(title = "2016 Trump Feeling Thermometer") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,300)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,100))
summary(anes_cleaned$V162079)
ggplot(data = anes_cleaned) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = V202144)) +
  labs(title = "2020 Trump Feeling Thermometer") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,300)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,100))
summary(anes_cleaned$V202144)
ggplot(data = anes_cleaned) +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = V242126)) +
  labs(title = "2024 Trump Feeling Thermometer") +  
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,300)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,100))
summary(anes_cleaned$V242126)
cat("2016 observations > 0 =",sum(anes_cleaned$V162079 > 0))
cat("2020 observations > 0  =", sum(anes_cleaned$V202144 > 0))
cat("2024 observations > 0  =", sum(anes_cleaned$V242126 > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
```
### Proportion by Gender
```{r}
mean_by_gender_2016 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V168307 > 0, V162079 > 0) %>%
  group_by(V168307) %>%
  summarise(count_2016 = n(), mean_2016 = mean(V162079), .groups = 'drop')
mean_by_gender_2020 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V168307 > 0, V202144 > 0) %>%
  group_by(V168307) %>%
  summarise(count_2020 = n(), mean_2020 = mean(V202144), .groups = 'drop')
mean_by_gender_2024 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V168307 > 0, V242126 > 0) %>%
  group_by(V168307) %>%
  summarise(count_2024 = n(), mean_2024 = mean(V242126), .groups = 'drop')
mean_2016 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V162079 > 0, V162079 > 0) %>%
  summarise(count_2016 = n(), mean_2016 = mean(V162079), .groups = 'drop')
mean_2020 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V162079 > 0, V202144 > 0) %>%
  summarise(count_2020 = n(), mean_2020 = mean(V202144), .groups = 'drop')
mean_2024 <- anes_cleaned %>%
  filter(V162079 > 0, V242126 > 0) %>%
  summarise(count_2024 = n(), mean_2024 = mean(V242126), .groups = 'drop')
mean_by_gender_2016; mean_by_gender_2020; mean_by_gender_2024; mean_2016; mean_2020; mean_2024
```

## Zack Descrpitives-

### Boxplot overtime

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

anes_plot <- anes_mergedfile_2016_2020_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    V162079 = ifelse(V162079 >= 1 & V162079 <= 100, V162079, NA),
    V202144 = ifelse(V202144 >= 1 & V202144 <= 100, V202144, NA),
    V242126 = ifelse(V242126 >= 1 & V242126 <= 100, V242126, NA)
  ) %>%
  select(V162079, V202144, V242126) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = recode(
      year,
      "V162079" = "2016",
      "V202144" = "2020",
      "V242126" = "2024"
    )
  )

ggplot(anes_plot, aes(x = year, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(1, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


### Frequency Plot Over Time

```{r}

anes_freq_20 <- anes_plot %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(
    therm_group = cut(
      value,
      breaks = c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100),
      labels = c("1-20", "21-40", "41-60", "61-80", "81-100")
    )
  ) %>%
  count(year, therm_group)

ggplot(anes_freq_20, aes(
  x = therm_group,
  y = year,
  size = n,
  color = year
)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name = "Frequency",
    range = c(3, 15)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Feeling Thermometer Score",
    y = "Year",
    color = "Year",
    title = "Feeling Thermometer Scores by Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
